questions.question:
Choose the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence:

(A) the winner

(B) declared

(C) was

(D) yesterday
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2)** i.e. **ACBD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject, "the winner," which is correctly indicated by **part (A).**
 
• Following the subject, "was declared" **(CB)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what happened to the winner.
 
• **The final part,** "yesterday" (ACBD) completes the sentence by providing the time reference.

Therefore, the correct answer is ACBD

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 2 (****CABD****):** This option starts with "was the winner declared yesterday," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect and confusing.
 
• **Option 3 (BCAD):** This option starts with "declared was the winner yesterday," which disrupts the logical flow of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 (CBAD):** This option starts with "was declared the winner yesterday," which is not a coherent sequence for this context.

questions.question:
Identify the correct type of sentence used in the line:

"at the heart of the debate lies a fundamental tension between technological progress and moral responsibility."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **simple sentence** contains a single independent clause (one subject + one predicate) and may include phrases but no subordinate clauses. (सरल वाक्य)
 
• The sentence *"At the heart of the debate lies a fundamental tension between technological progress and moral responsibility."* has one main clause: **subject phrase** ("a fundamental tension") and **predicate** ("lies").
 
• The phrase *"At the heart of the debate"* is an introductory prepositional phrase and *"between technological progress and moral responsibility"* is a prepositional phrase adding detail — neither forms an additional clause.
 
• Because there is only one independent clause and no subordinate or coordinate clauses, the sentence is best classified as **simple**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Compound** – Requires two or more independent clauses joined by a conjunction; not present here.
 
• **Option 2: Complex** – Requires at least one subordinate clause; the sentence has none.
 
• **Option 4: Compound-Complex** – Requires multiple independent clauses and at least one subordinate clause; not applicable.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

She said, "O that I were a bird!"

options.text: She said that she wished she were a bird
She said that she has been a bird.
She said that she wanted to be a bird.
She said that she was a bird.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she wished she were a bird.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"O that I were a bird!" becomes "she wished she were a bird"**
 
 
• The exclamatory phrase "O that" is converted to "she wished" to express the desire in indirect speech.
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
• Verb "were" remains unchanged as it expresses an unreal or hypothetical condition.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Reporting verb "said" remains the same, as it introduces the exclamation.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Exclamatory "O that" is removed in indirect speech.
 
• Sentence is formatted as a statement without exclamatory punctuation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said that she wished she were a bird."*

• Incorrect tense: "has been" implies a completed action, which does not align with the original sentence's hypothetical desire.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said that she wanted to be a bird."
 
 
• Incorrect verb: "wanted" changes the meaning to a past desire instead of a hypothetical wish.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said that she was a bird."
 
 
• Incorrect meaning: "was a bird" implies a statement of fact, not a wish or hypothetical condition.
